messages:
Anya K: follow-up from the paged-kv + attention-kernel RFC — we ran into a few compatibility edge cases during the prototype. want to capture requirements before we lock kernels.
Matt P: yep. what were the specific gotchas you hit?
Anya K: two surfaced: 1) kernels that assume contiguous KV for inner-loop matmuls break when we serve fragmented pages. 2) eviction/compaction pauses cause latency spikes if kernel expects stable pointers.
Sophie L: for (1) is the kernel failing outright, or just slower?
Anya K: failing in one optimized fused-attn kernel (it memrefs KV as a contiguous buffer). another kernel handled scatter-gather but ~20% slower.
Raul G: that matches hardware tradeoffs. contiguous wins for bandwidth and vectorized loads. scatter needs gather kernels or pre-copy.
Matt P: we should define a minimal kernel contract: either "requires_contiguous_kv" or "supports_paged_kv". runtime picks a kernel or does a copy-to-contig step.
Sophie L: agree. add a cost model cost_copy(bytes) so scheduler can decide when copy is worth it.
Anya K: proposed kernel metadata fields:
```
kernel_caps: {
  contiguous_kv: bool,
  max_contiguous_tokens: int,
  supports_gather: bool,
  preferred_alignment: int,
}
```
Matt P: nice. also need pin/unpin semantics for pages used by kernels that hold refs across calls (e.g., caching layers).
Raul G: +1. pin should prevent eviction and compaction for the pinned lifetime. pin must be cheap (inc refcount) and unpin triggers async GC.
Sophie L: question: do we allow kernel-level compaction hints? e.g., kernel says "I will hold this layer's KV pinned for N requests" so runtime can avoid copies.
Anya K: we prototyped a PinHandle that includes expected_duration_tokens and a hint bit. runtime uses hint to avoid moving those pages during compaction window.
Matt P: evictions: we need an LRU-ish global policy but layered by "hotness" per model & layer. fragmentation occurs when we evict small pages from many layers.
Raul G: compaction strategy: background compaction that coalesces free slots when fragmentation > threshold. but compaction cannot move pinned pages.
Sophie L: threshold numbers? in prototype we used fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 or free_runs > 128 -> schedule compaction. happy to tune.
Anya K: perf numbers: with scattered access + gather-kernel we saw +22% CPU and +18% latency p95. copying into contiguous buffer costs ~5-7% CPU but avoids kernel changes.
Matt P: so runtime heuristic: if kernel.contiguous_kv==true and expected_tokens > copy_break_even -> copy; else use gather if kernel supports it.
Raul G: also account for memory pressure. copy increases transient memory. if mem_free < mem_threshold avoid copy and pick gather kernel.
Sophie L: we should expose metrics to console: page_fragmentation_ratio, pinned_pages_count, compaction_queue_len, avg_copy_bytes. ops will love that.
Anya K: agreed. action items:
- Matt: draft kernel metadata PR (caps + cost hints) — due Thu
- Raul: design pin/unpin + GC state machine + compaction heuristic doc — due Tue
- Sophie: add console metrics + alert when compaction backlog > 5 — due Fri
InfraBot: CI pipeline: build/bench/paged-kv-tests started (run id ci-8721)
Anya K: one more question: do we allow per-customer pin policies? enterprise might want long pins for latency-sensitivity.
Matt P: support it via per-tenant quotas: pinned_tokens_limit and pin_ttl defaults. we'll enforce via admission control.
Raul G: note: long pins worsen fragmentation if tenant holds many small pins. we should expose a fragmentation charge to tenant billing if they request sticky pins.
Sophie L: ok. i'll mock dashboard rows for pinned usage and fragmentation charge.
Anya K: thanks team. if no objections i'll write RFC follow-up with kernel caps + pin API + compaction sketch. tagging for visibility: @Matt P @Sophie L @Raul G :thumbsup
__notes: This thread is a brief RFC follow-up discussion about paged KV fragmentation, eviction, kernel compatibility. Messages are short as in Slack style.
